title: Human Sexuality & Gender Identity Explained
description:
What makes someone male, female, or anything in between? Most people think it’s simple: XY = male, XX = female. But modern genetics and neuroscience tell a far more fascinating and complex story.

This video unpacks the science of sex determination and human sexuality:

How the SRY gene on the Y chromosome activates SOX9, suppressing female traits.
How errors in this process can result in an XY person with female organs or an XX person with male organs.
Why the brain and the body don’t always align — differences in the hypothalamus, amygdala, hippocampus, and brain stem can make someone’s gender identity different from their biological sex.
How hormones and genetics shape sexual orientation, creating diversity in attraction.
Why homosexuality is as natural as left-handedness, and not a disease or choice.

We also dive into history and culture:
Ancient Indian texts like the Kama Sutra and depictions in Khajuraho temples show homosexuality existed and was acknowledged.
The Sushruta Samhita even said homosexuality is unchangeable.
Colonial-era morality and modern religious dogma created stigma, but science dismantles these myths.

If you’ve searched for male vs female genetics, human sexuality explained, SRY gene, homosexuality science, or gender identity facts, this video gives you the actual scien perspective.

Like, comment, share, and hype this video to spread awareness and counter pseudoscience and prejudice.

06:20 – Brain Wiring and Gender Identity
08:40 – Hormones and Sexual Orientation
11:00 – Homosexuality: Natural, Not a Choice
